title: Potassium + Digoxin = Deadly Combo
hook: This lab value kills faster than any other — do you check it first?
scenario: Your patient is on digoxin. Their potassium is 3.2. They report nausea and have premature ventricular contractions on the monitor. What's your FIRST action?
answer: Check potassium BEFORE giving digoxin. Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity risk. Hold the dose, notify provider, and prepare for potassium replacement.
payoff: Rule: ALWAYS check K+ before digoxin. Hypokalemia = increased toxicity. Hyperkalemia = also dangerous. Potassium is never 'just a number'.
caption:
🚨 NCLEX Trap of the Day: Potassium + Digoxin

This combo kills more patients than you think.

Your patient on digoxin has K+ 3.2 and PVCs. FIRST action?

A) Give digoxin as scheduled
B) Hold digoxin, check K+, notify provider
C) Give potassium supplement only
D) Call rapid response

Answer: B

Hypokalemia INCREASES digoxin toxicity. Always check K+ first.
